name: Generative Scheduling
tagline: A resource-loaded, logic-linked schedule generated from the scope, with durations and crews computed rather than guessed.
problem: Schedules are built by hand from linear templates, assume people are fully available to one project, and miss the third-party dependencies that cascade through engineering into construction.
how: Scope, quantities, the 3D model, crew data and comparable schedules
Generates activities and logic, computes parametric durations and resources, links each activity to the model, and optimizes the sequence
A resource-levelled, model-linked schedule with P50 and P80 dates, ready for P6
features: Generated from scope: Activities and logic from the work breakdown and comparable schedules
Parametric durations: Computed from quantities, productivity rates and conditions
Parametric resources: Crews, equipment and people across projects, without 100% utilization assumptions
Linked to the 3D model: Each activity tied to model elements for the 4D build
Third-party dependencies: Permits, land, utilities and owner deliverables modelled as logic
Multi-objective optimizer: A genetic algorithm searches non-linear, resource-constrained sequences; Monte Carlo simulation tests each option as faster, cheaper or safer
Schedule risk: Monte Carlo P50 and P80 dates
Export: Primavera P6 and Microsoft Project
Planner companion: Reads each activity as the planner writes it, and flags logic gaps early
Schedule quality: Logic and quality checked before optimization
